ABOUT ORBITE

◌

Places to drift through.
Places to listen in.

ORBITE is a generative cinema studio that runs entirely in your browser. Twelve imaginary landscapes are drawn in real time, new places appear with every draw, and each landscape is also an acoustic place.

The sound is Loopra Stage: thirty-two independent loops in one shared key, every layer sitting at its own distance between your ears and the horizon. Loops of different lengths keep meeting in new ways, and no pass is ever the same take. Drop your own music onto the studio to let it travel through the landscape instead.

Image and sound made here
No model to downloadBuilt on a Mac mini
M4 Pro · 64 GB

Landscapes are procedural and the sound is synthesized: no AI service is called and nothing leaves your browser. Video exports use the format your browser supports.

STUDIO NOTES

Listening to Thursday Afternoon

In a 1985 interview, Brian Eno describes piano notes returning at different intervals and timbres shaped by tape speed. ORBITE offers an original interpretation: thirty-two independent cycles, long resonances, and a continuous bed of sound.

Read the 1985 interview ↗

A few gestures.

Space
Pause / resume the image
S
A new surprise
M
Play / pause the sound
F
A world in fullscreen
1 — 9, 0, − =
Change destination
Pointer
Gently shift your view

Drop an audio file onto the studio to add your soundtrack. The notebook keeps your places and settings, including loop lengths and the layers you chose. The harmonic pad is the foundation and has a level of its own, starting at 70 %. Each world arrives with its own key, space and layers; press KEEP to carry your sound settings from world to world. Click a reel to mute a layer, or ↻ for new lengths. Staging puts every layer at its own distance, from your ears to the horizon; Walking lets them drift slowly. The arrows trigger a portamento call.

One sound, a new elsewhere.
